*This is a **template** — a page somebody wrote out in advance, which GitHub put in front of you when you clicked "New issue". Nothing in it is fixed. Replace the italic lines with your own words, and delete any heading that does not apply.*

*What you are writing is called an **issue**. On this repo we call it what it is: a **work order**. One job, described well enough that somebody else — a person or an agent — can do it without coming back to ask what you meant.*

**One rule before you start.** If you state a requirement anywhere below — a TxDOT rule, a statute, an accuracy tolerance, a notice period, a fee — put the citation and its link beside it. This is not bureaucracy. A work order on this repo once stated a rule that was not true, and four pages repeated it before anyone noticed. The account is at [The claim we got wrong](https://ricksmith.github.io/survey-recon/managing-your-agent/the-claim-we-got-wrong/).

---

## Why

*Why this job is worth doing, and what goes wrong if nobody does it. Write this part first. If you cannot say why, the work order is not ready to hand to anybody.*

## What

*What to build or change. Name files and folders where you can. Bullet points are fine — this does not have to read like prose.*

## Acceptance criteria

*How anyone can tell the job is finished. Write each one so it can be answered yes or no by looking at the result, rather than by asking the person who did the work.*

- [ ] 
- [ ] 
- [ ] 

## Out of scope

*What this work order deliberately does not cover. This is the heading that stops a small job quietly becoming a large one.*

## Blocked by

*Other work orders that have to finish first. Write them as `#12` and GitHub links them for you. Write "None — can start immediately" if nothing is in the way.*

## Notes

*Anything the person doing the work would want to know before they start. A trap, a source, a link to the manual section, a decision already made and the reason for it. Delete this heading if there is nothing.*
